notes: RECALL TIE AGAIN: assertion pass rate 100% in BOTH arms (23/23) on the HARD set, run on Sonnet. Both caught every subtle planted vuln — JWT kid->key-swap, TOCTOU/idempotency races, bcrypt 72-byte truncation, non-constant-time secure_compare, PBKDF2-1000, the bypassable SSRF blocklist, the prefix path-containment bug, blacklist stored-XSS.
THOROUGHNESS FAVORS BASELINE: total real findings with_skill=29 TP vs without_skill=33 TP. The baseline surfaced MORE legitimate issues (payments +1, fetcher +2, files +1), not fewer.

PRECISION ~TIE (thin skill edge): with_skill precision 1.0 (29TP/0FP) vs without_skill 0.971 (33TP/1FP). The skill's ONLY measurable benefit across 10 reviews was 1 avoided false positive (eval-0). Single-run, so within noise.
COST: with_skill mean 102,814 tokens vs 79,561 (x1.29); time x1.06. Smaller premium than iter-1 because Sonnet baselines were themselves thorough/slow.

CROSS-ITERATION CONCLUSION: across 2 model tiers (frontier iter-1, Sonnet iter-2) and 2 difficulty levels, security-checklists produced NO measurable recall/thoroughness gain and only a razor-thin, noise-level precision edge, at 1.3-1.8x cost. For capable models the skill's exhaustive pattern lists appear to be recall the model already has. Highest-leverage improvement hypothesis: the load-bearing parts are the Exploitability Discipline (precision) + output contract + the genuinely rare checks; the bulk pattern enumeration is the trim candidate. Value for WEAK models (e.g. Haiku) and output CONSISTENCY remain untested and are the likely real justification.
